steps.message:
You are a hydrogeologist preparing site notes for a borehole drilling team.

Station H-04 (survey area H). Interpreted VES layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 133.9 | 19.46 | 19.46
2 | 50.7 | 19.69 | 39.15
3 | 23.0 | 4.00 | 43.15
4 | 61.9 | 4.32 | 47.47
5 | 20.8 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this sounding curve as QHA-type.

Write the site note using exactly this template:

Station: <station name>
Curve type: <VES curve type>
Aquifer depth: <depth range in m>
Recommendation: <one or two sentences for the drilling team>

Reference note: Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station: H-04
Curve type: QHK (recalculated from the resistivity sequence — layers 1-2-3 give Q [133.9>50.7>23.0], layers 2-3-4 give H [50.7>23.0<61.9], layers 3-4-5 give K [23.0<61.9>20.8]; this supersedes the QHA label on file, which appears to be a transcription error)
Aquifer depth: below 47.47 m (Layer 5, ρ = 20.8 Ω·m, is the thick, laterally extensive low-resistivity unit at the base of the section and is the most likely water-bearing horizon; the thin 23 Ω·m zone at 39.15–43.15 m is probably only a clay lens)
Recommendation: Plan the borehole to penetrate at least 60–65 m to adequately test and screen the Layer 5 conductive zone below 47.47 m; case off the overlying resistive cap (Layer 4, 61.9 Ω·m) and confirm lithology with cuttings/geophysical logging, as the 4 m clay-like layer at ~39–43 m should be treated as a confining bed rather than the target aquifer.
